body:
[A10] Assignment for #190 (author [A654]). The declaration is built in milan-fpga, not in the processor: `hdl/milan/milan_datapath.sv:8201` and `:5641`. The fix is therefore a milan-fpga PR, branch `190-crf-maxframesize` from dev e9cbb676, and it closes this issue by cross-reference.

1. First cite the CRF TSpec MaxFrameSize that the Milan Base Audio Formats specification and Milan v1.2 4.3.3.2 Table 4.4 assign to the DUT's CRF format. Read them under $WORKSPACE_HOME/standards.
2. Otherwise derive it from the CRF PDU the DUT sends: the timestamps per PDU and the header (IEEE 1722-2016 Clause 10). It must cover the largest frame sent (IEEE 802.1Q-2018 35.2.2.8.4).
3. Set the declared value to it, derived from the format parameters, not mirrored as a constant.
4. Add a suite case that pins the TSpec value against the PDU size, with a planted mutant.
5. Run every gate the change touches, all rc 0.
6. STOP if the derived value differs from the specified one and the difference cannot be traced.

Put your receipts in the output directory, with an index generated from the files present. Post REVIEW READY or STOP here.

[A654] TAKEN
Branch: kebag-logic/milan-fpga `190-crf-maxframesize` from dev e9cbb676
Authoritative references: Milan v1.2 4.3.3.2 Table 4.4 (CRF, 1 ts/pdu row) and 7.3.2 / Table 7.1; IEEE 1722-2016 Clause 10; IEEE 802.1Q-2018 35.2.2.8.4; assignment comment 6256483038
Interpreted scope: make the CRF Stream Output's Talker Advertise declare the CRF MaxFrameSize derived from the CRF format parameters (timestamps per PDU, Clause 10 header, the Table 4.4 extra octet) instead of the AAF value, and pin it with a suite case and planted mutant.
Validation plan: the touched Verilator suites (pp_shadow / milan_dp) with the pinned Verilator, the docs and rtl-fast gates the change touches, all rc 0.
Blockers: none yet

[A654] STOP
Head: kebag-logic/milan-fpga `190-crf-maxframesize` = e9cbb676d7fdd6539aa408e5dfe38870a4ae1a5f (no commits; nothing changed)
Value: the specified CRF MaxFrameSize is 29 (Milan v1.2 4.3.3.2 Table 4.4, row CRF 1 ts/pdu; 7.3.2 / Table 7.1 give one timestamp per PDU). The derivation agrees: the IEEE 1722-2016 10.4.1 header is 20 octets, plus one 8-octet timestamp (10.4.13), which equals the DUT's 28-octet CRF AVTPDU (`KL_crf_tx.sv:194,197`), plus the extra octet from the Table 4.4 note, giving 29. Item 6 is NOT triggered.
Blocker: the assignment's premise that this is a milan-fpga-only fix does not hold. The parent passes ONE scalar (`milan_datapath.sv:8201`, `tctx_maxf_w[0]` = 24*8+25 = 217, the AAF row). At `protocol_processor_top.sv:2700` (pin 2cbed0a9, and the same on current main), every source's engine-driven DECLARE_TALKER captures that scalar, and the service path that could carry a different value is tied off (`KL_pp_shadow.sv:1285-1293`). The parent cannot make the CRF source declare 29 while the AAF sources keep 24N+25. Rejected alternatives: drive the scalar with 29 (AAF under-reservation); switch it in the parent (the parent cannot see which source a gate open belongs to); re-declare through the service path (the wrong TSpec is on the wire first, and it races the engine); edit the processor submodule in this lane (that is another repository's lane).
Decision needed: approve a processor change to a per-source engine TSpec MaxFrameSize (for example `cfg_tspec_max_frame_i[N_STREAM_OUT_P*16-1:0]` indexed by the gate's source, the same shape as `cfg_stream_id_i`). A parent lane would then adopt that pin, drive the CRF slot with 20 + 8*timestamps_per_pdu + 1 derived from the CRF constants, and add a suite case pinning it against the PDU length with a planted mutant. That lane should also correct the stale comment at `KL_crf_tx.sv:206-211`, which still says 42.
Evidence: kept with the lane receipts: repository state, standards sha256, the line-by-line code trace, and the computed derivation, which also shows the issue's over-reservation: 16.576 against 5.632 Mb/s, a gap of 10.944 Mb/s.

[A10] Ruling on the STOP (6256554371, [A654]). The value is settled: **29**. It is Milan v1.2 4.3.3.2 Table 4.4's CRF row at 1 timestamp per PDU (7.3.2, Table 7.1). It equals the IEEE 1722-2016 10.4.1 header of 20 octets, plus one 8-octet timestamp (10.4.13), plus the Table 4.4 note's extra octet, and it matches the DUT's 28-octet CRF AVTPDU.

The fix needs the processor change the lane identified, and it is approved. The engine-driven DECLARE_TALKER takes its TSpec MaxFrameSize per source: `cfg_tspec_max_frame_i[N_STREAM_OUT_P*16-1:0]`, indexed like `cfg_stream_id_i`. That replaces the single scalar captured at `protocol_processor_top.sv:2700`, and the tied-off service path at `KL_pp_shadow.sv:1285-1293` follows.

The port change is approved for this issue only. Two parts:
1. **Processor PR, this issue:** the per-source port, every DECLARE_TALKER using its source's value, and suite cases for two sources with different values, each with a planted mutant. The processor gates pass, and so do the parent consumer gates on a scratch parent that drives the new port with the old scalar on every slot, which means no behaviour change in the parent yet.
2. **Parent change, which rides the next pin adoption:** drive the CRF slot with 20 + 8 × timestamps_per_pdu + 1, derived from the CRF constants, and the AAF slots as today. Add a suite case pinning it against the PDU length, with a planted mutant, and correct the stale comment at `KL_crf_tx.sv:206-211`.

The lane runs part 1 now, from processor main. Part 2 goes into the adoption lane's assignment.

[A654] TAKEN
Branch: processor `190-per-source-tspec` from main 5addf29759a22372ed6aa3e1d52a3aad29e3ecd7
Authoritative references: ruling 6256563927 (PART 1 only); IEEE 802.1Q-2018 35.2.2.8.4; Milan v1.2 4.3.3.2 Table 4.4
Interpreted scope: replace the scalar `cfg_tspec_max_frame_i[15:0]` with the approved per-source `cfg_tspec_max_frame_i[N_STREAM_OUT_P*16-1:0]`, indexed like `cfg_stream_id_i`, so every engine-driven DECLARE_TALKER captures its own source's MaxFrameSize (`protocol_processor_top.sv:2700`); suite cases for two sources with different values, each with a planted mutant; the docs that record the port. No register-map change and no other port or parameter change.
Validation plan: every processor suite, lint, make check, gen_matrix --check, syn/yosys/run.sh and every campaign that builds the top, at base and head; parent consumer gates on an uncommitted scratch parent that drives every slot with the old scalar (no parent behaviour change).
Blockers: none yet

[A654] REVIEW READY
Head: processor `190-per-source-tspec` = 90321bffbf48a271e9862cad92973bd862827d5f (one commit on main 5addf297; not pushed, no PR opened)
Scope: ruling 6256563927, part 1 only. `cfg_tspec_max_frame_i` is now `[N_STREAM_OUT_P*16-1:0]`, flat `[16*s +: 16]` like `cfg_stream_id_i` (`protocol_processor_top.sv:300-303`). Every engine-driven DECLARE_TALKER (gate open and gate close) captures its own source's slot (`:2703`). No other port, parameter or register-map change. The service face was already per request.
Tests: new `tb/pp_top` section TS on a fresh model, whose eight slots are eight different Milan v1.2 Table 4.4 values (source 0 the AAF 217, source 1 the CRF 29, sources 2-7 the AAF value at 2-7 channels). TS0: every source's DA gate is open. TS1 ×8: each source's Talker attribute on the MSRP wire declares its own slot, range-matched per 802.1Q-2018 35.2.2.8. Arms in `tb/pp_top/acmp_mutants.py`, all KILLED: `tspec_slot_zero` (fails source 1's check, got 217), `tspec_slot_last` (fails source 0's, got 193), `tspec_no_allocator` (fails TS0). The main model keeps 1024 on every slot, so no existing check moves.
Gates, base 5addf297 vs head, all rc 0: run_suites 1,030,013 → 1,030,022 (only pp_top +9); lint_hdl, make check, gen_matrix --check and syn/yosys/run.sh identical (make check: +4 links). Every campaign that builds the top or tb/pp_top is identical, except that acmp_mutants goes 51/51 → 54/54 (the three new arms).
Parent consumer gates: scratch parent at dev e9cbb676, gitlink staged, the two earlier lanes' patches, plus at head a scratch-only patch driving every slot with the old scalar. 23 of 24 rc 0 at base and head with identical records. `check_submodule_docs` fails identically at both (documented pin differs). Without the every-slot patch, `lint_rtl` fails at `KL_pp_shadow.sv:1161` (WIDTHEXPAND), so the adoption must drive the wide port.
Not closed by this: the CRF stream declaring 29 is part 2 (the parent adoption). The PR body says "Refs #190".
To confirm: the brief's E_SCFG scope line and its "Closes #179" item came from #179's template; I read the scope as #190 part 1 and left #179 out.
Evidence: kept with the lane receipts (HANDOFF, PR body, per-gate records, hash list).
